questions.q: What constitutional principle guarantees that every adult citizen in India has the right to vote for their Lok Sabha representative?
questions.a: Universal Adult Suffrage (Article 326). A wrong answer usually confuses this with indirect election methods or eligibility age, revealing a misunderstanding of how direct popular sovereignty operates in the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: Why is the Lok Sabha referred to as the "House of the People" rather than a council of states or appointed delegates?
questions.a: It is called the House of the People because its members are directly elected by ordinary citizens of India, ensuring direct accountability to the electorate. A wrong answer claiming members are chosen by state assemblies confuses the Lok Sabha with the Rajya Sabha.

questions.q: A citizen living in a rural constituency turns 18 years old just before the general elections. Can they cast a vote to elect their Member of Parliament for the Lok Sabha?
questions.a: Yes. Under Article 326 of the Constitution, any Indian citizen who is 18 years of age or older, and not otherwise disqualified, has the right to vote in Lok Sabha elections. A wrong answer suggests the student does not understand universal adult suffrage or age eligibility.

questions.q: How does the territorial constituency system ensure that densely populated states like Uttar Pradesh have more Lok Sabha seats than smaller states like Sikkim?
questions.a: Constituencies are carved out based on population size so that roughly equal numbers of citizens are represented by each MP, giving more populous states a higher seat count. A wrong answer indicates confusion between equal state representation and proportional popular representation.

questions.q: Does the direct election of Lok Sabha members make the government more accountable to citizens compared to a system with appointed lawmakers?
questions.a: Yes, because elected officials must face the voters every five years, forcing them to address public welfare and citizen concerns to win reelection. A wrong answer shows a lack of understanding of democratic accountability and electoral consequences.

questions.q: Design a short rule for a mock school parliament explaining how your school would elect a "Student Lok Sabha" if it mirrored the Indian national legislature.
questions.a: A good response proposes direct, secret-ballot voting by all students (representing citizens) divided into equal grade-based constituencies. A poor response suggests teachers appointing representatives, missing the core requirement of direct election.
